correctness.rationale: The published endemic-equilibrium polynomial is \(C_0 I_h^2+C_1 I_h+C_2=0\), with \(C_0>0\) in the saturated-treatment regime and \(C_2\) equal to a positive factor times \(1-\mathcal R_0^2\). Vieta's formulas therefore give the complete positive-root classification. If \(\mathcal R_0>1\), the root product is negative and exactly one root is positive. At threshold, the nonzero root is positive exactly when \(C_1<0\). If \(\mathcal R_0<1\), real roots have the same sign and are positive exactly when \(C_1<0\); two distinct positive roots require \(\Delta>0\), while \(\Delta=0\) is the sole unique-positive-root fold. The paper's Lemma 3.1 prints mutually inconsistent subthreshold bullets. The exact witness \(\mu_h=\mu_v=\delta_h=\gamma=u=\alpha_1=\alpha_2=\beta_2=\Lambda_v=1\), \(b=100\), \(\Lambda_h=10\), \(\beta_1=29/100\) gives \(\mathcal R_0^2=29/30\), \(C_0=658\), \(C_1=-8013/100\), \(C_2=1/10\), and positive discriminant, so two positive endemic roots exist and reconstruct positive equilibria of the original equations.
residual_risks: The result classifies endemic-equilibrium existence/multiplicity, not stability of the two subthreshold equilibria.

The result is a source-specific correction with exact root conditions, not merely a rediscovery that backward bifurcation can occur.
